candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply current CDC glove and gown recommendations for Contact Precautions without overgeneralizing gown use.

options.A: Wear a respirator for every room entry and omit gloves.
options.B: Put on gloves upon room entry; wear a gown upon entry when clothing contact with the client or potentially contaminated environmental surfaces is anticipated.
options.C: Use gloves only after visible body-fluid contamination occurs.
options.D: Wear a sterile gown and sterile gloves for every interaction regardless of anticipated contact.

candidate.rationale: CDC Contact Precautions direct health-care personnel to don gloves upon entry. A gown is donned upon entry when clothing contact with the client or potentially contaminated environmental surfaces is anticipated; this is more precise than asserting a gown is required for every entry in all circumstances.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Contact Precautions include gloves on entry and gown use when clothing contact with the client or contaminated environment is anticipated.
candidate.source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Contact Precautions
candidate.source_locator: Section V.B.3.a and V.B.3.b.i — glove and gown use for Contact Precautions
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A client is on Contact Precautions. Which PPE practice is consistent with current CDC isolation guidance?
